lines: 6-month history of recurrent abdominal pain and altered bowel habits

She reports that her abdominal pain is crampy in nature, located in the lower quadrants, and often relieved by defecation.
She has alternating periods of diarrhea and constipation.
She denies any recent travel, use of antibiotics, or consumption of unusual foods.
She has tried increasing her dietary fiber intake without significant relief.
- Ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel 30 mcg/150 mcg orally daily
She denies any family history of gastrointestinal diseases.
On physical examination, her abdomen is soft, non-distended, with no masses or organomegaly palpable.
There is mild tenderness in the lower abdominal quadrants without rebound or guarding.
Rectal examination is normal with no blood noted.

encounters.cc: 6-month history of intermittent abdominal discomfort related to work stress

lines: 6-month history of intermittent abdominal discomfort related to work stress

The patient is a 35-year-old female with established irritable bowel syndrome previously evaluated in Gastroenterology in 2020 and 2021 and Internal Medicine in 2022 who presents to Psychiatry with a 6-month history of intermittent abdominal discomfort related to work stress.
She reports episodes of crampy lower abdominal pain that worsen during periods of work-related stress and improve after having a bowel movement.
The pain is often accompanied by bloating and fluctuates between days of loose stools and other times when she feels constipated and has to strain.
She denies nocturnal symptoms, weight loss, hematochezia, or mucus in the stool.
Her appetite is normal, and she reports no history of recent infections or travel.
She works in a high-pressure marketing job and states that her symptoms flare most when deadlines are tight or when she feels anxious.
She has tried cutting back on dairy, but this has not improved her symptoms.
She takes she takes an oral contraceptive.
- Ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel 30 mcg/150 mcg orally daily
She has no family history of colon cancer or inflammatory bowel disease.
Physical examination reveals mild tenderness in the lower quadrants, but no rebound, guarding, or palpable masses.
Laboratory testing, including complete blood count, ESR, CRP, and tissue transglutaminase IgA, are all within normal limits.
A basic metabolic panel and thyroid function tests are also normal.

lines: Severe diffuse abdominal pain progressively worsening over 24 hours

She reports that the pain is diffuse, non-radiating, and has been progressively worsening over the past 24 hours.
She denies any nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or fever.
Despite analgesics, she continues to report severe pain.

encounters.cc: Sudden-onset shortness of breath and left-sided chest pain

lines: Sudden-onset shortness of breath and left-sided chest pain

The patient is a 39-year-old female with irritable bowel syndrome and factitious disorder imposed on self who returns to the emergency department with sudden-onset shortness of breath and left-sided chest pain that began two hours ago.
The pain is sharp, worse with inspiration, and does not radiate.
She has no cough, fever, or sputum production.
She returned from a 14-hour international flight two days ago and has been feeling generally well until this morning.
Her only medication is a combined oral contraceptive pill, which she has taken for the past five years
- Ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel 30 mcg/150 mcg orally daily
Respiratory rate is 22/min, heart rate is 108/min, and oxygen saturation is 93% on room air
She appears mildly anxious but is alert and oriented.
Lung auscultation is clear bilaterally, and cardiac exam reveals no murmurs, gallops, or rubs.
There is no leg swelling, erythema, or calf tenderness.
ABG on room air shows decreased PaO₂ with a normal chest x-ray. D-dimer is elevated.
A chest x-ray shows clear lung fields and normal cardiac silhouette.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset of right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking

lines: Sudden onset of right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking
Patient is a 40-year-old female with factitious disorder imposed on self and pulmonary embolism presenting with neurological symptoms beginning 2 hours ago while eating dinner.
She reports choking on a piece of meat earlier this evening but did not seek immediate medical attention.
Her past medical history is significant for migraines and oral contraceptive use.
- Ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel 30 mcg/150 mcg orally daily
Her blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg, heart rate is 78 beats per minute, and temperature is 37.2°C (99.0°F).
On examination, she has a right-sided facial droop, aphasia, and hemiplegia.
A neurological examination confirms expressive aphasia and right upper and lower extremity weakness with a National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of 15.
A non-contrast head CT scan is negative for hemorrhage.
Carotid duplex ultrasound shows no evidence of significant atherosclerotic disease.
